body:
To accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support. _Hey team – it's Gov. Andy Beshear. My friend, Amy Klobuchar, just announced her campaign for Governor of Minnesota. Below, she outlines her powerful story, and why her leadership is needed in this state, now more than ever. Minnesota is a critical state that we must keep blue in 2026. Will you take a moment to read her message, and then, commit to joining her campaign today?_

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124300178/598185044/2128552367?refcode=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&&&&utm_campaign=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&&&&utm_medium=email&&&&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQ0ZjFiNmUtNTFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gGAd6EtvH-p1DnfHwkL5plMrY1VPw6mkkU2DzY9fRKA=)

Peter --

I wanted you to be one of the first to hear the news: I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota. **This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other.**

**[I’m going to tell you why in a moment. But first: Will you help us get off to a strong start by splitting a donation between Gov. Andy Beshear's In This Together PAC and my campaign?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124300179/598185045/2128552367?refcode=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&&&&utm_campaign=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&&&&utm_medium=email&&&&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQ0ZjFiNmUtNTFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gGAd6EtvH-p1DnfHwkL5plMrY1VPw6mkkU2DzY9fRKA=)**

I’m not going to sugar coat it -- Minnesota has been through a lot.

The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. Three thousand ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America’s heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will.

**These moments call for grit and resilience.** I’ve learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up.

And grit? I learned that from my family. I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn’t be where I am today without them.

**These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state.

I led our state’s biggest prosecutors’ office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law.

**I will do my job without fear or favor. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful. That’s what I did as prosecutor. That’s what I did as senator. And that’s what I will do as your governor.**

I believe we must stand up for what’s right. And fix what’s wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love.

And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder.

_But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support._

**This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change.**

**[So please: Will you support my campaign for governor with a donation today? Your contribution will be split with In This Together PAC.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124300180/598185046/2128552367?refcode=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&&&&utm_campaign=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&&&&utm_medium=email&&&&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQ0ZjFiNmUtNTFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gGAd6EtvH-p1DnfHwkL5plMrY1VPw6mkkU2DzY9fRKA=)**

**I like my job in the Senate. But I love our state more than any job.** I love the people of Minnesota. And Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor.

Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us.

To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do -- and that’s why I’m asking you to join us.

Amy _Prepared and Paid for by Minnesotans for Klobuchar_ | | **Andy and In This Together PAC are working to support leaders who will lead with compassion and decency, reject anger politics, and always do what's right. Will you donate today to support In This Together's mission?** [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124300181/598185047/2128552367?refcode=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260129_MNgov_fndt_gq_act___AK_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=1d4f1b6e-51fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWQ0ZjFiNmUtNTFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=gGAd6EtvH-p1DnfHwkL5plMrY1VPw6mkkU2DzY9fRKA=)

Peter,

It's our first end-of-month deadline of 2026, and we've officially had Donald Trump back in the Oval Office for a full year now.

_And what an eventful year it's been..._

In just twelve months, we've seen how much damage can be done when chaos, corruption, cruelty, and a quest for absolute power go unchecked.

We've seen reckless decisions that cost people their jobs, sky-high tariffs that raise prices for families already stretched thin, and unqualified extremists like RFK Jr. elevated into positions of power.

In recent days we’ve seen Trump weaponize his personal brutal police force, ICE, in American cities. | | The masked goons who call themselves “ICE” are terrorizing our communities, Peter, and it’s got to stop. Last week they detained five year old Liam Ramos. Over the weekend, six ICE agents held down and killed Alex Pretti for holding a camera in his hand. This is Donald Trump’s America, and the blood of every life lost because of ICE is on this Administration’s hands. I want to be VERY clear: **When the DHS funding bill hit the Senate floor today, I voted NO — not another penny for ICE.** We are in an affordability crisis. While folks struggle to put food on the table and find healthcare coverage, Republicans are misappropriating their taxpayer dollars to fund the killing of Americans. We are also in an accountability crisis. The people allowing this terror and committing these acts of violence aren’t held accountable whatsoever for violating the law. _I urge all of my Republican colleagues to stand up to this Administration and say, no more. No more killing innocent Americans on the streets. No more funding for this lawless organization._ Every Senator owes it to the American people to speak out on the atrocities ICE is committing. We cannot give more power to Kristi Noem and Donald Trump to reign terror on our communities. The right side of history here is obvious, and I will continue to use my voice and position to do what’s best for America and Maryland. Together, Angela Alsobrooks

subject: Hoping you had a Merry Christmas and Happy New Year

body:
| | | | A Christmas note from our family as we reflect on the year and look forward to 2026.
---
A Christmas note from our family as we reflect on the season. Peter, We hope this note finds you well. We enjoyed the holidays. Twenty-one family joined us at our home on Pewaukee Lake this Christmas. What a joy to have our sons and daughters-in-law, their families, my brother's family, a grandnephew and grandniece, cousins, and my mother. It has been wonderful to have everyone together for Christmas and throughout the holidays! We took the kids on a memorable trip for Tonette's birthday this year. It was great, but we always appreciate coming back home to the United States. As we prepare to celebrate the 250th anniversary of our beloved republic, we are even more grateful to our founders for the freedoms we hold dear today. This coming 4th of July will be about celebrating more than a birthday. It is worth acknowledging our independence from the government, rather than our dependence on it. In the same way, Christmas is about far more than special gifts and family gatherings. For us, it is about remembering that God loved us so much that he sent his one and only Son as a baby, who grew and taught, and ultimately died on the cross for our sins. Gloriously, he rose from the grave. For those who follow him, Jesus offers eternal life. That is the ultimate gift! We hope you had a Merry Christmas and a happy New Year,
**Scott and Tonette**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: “Do right and risk the consequences”
body:
This Sam Houston quote is one of my favorites.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
**“Do right and risk the consequences.”**
This quote from Sam Houston, one of the first Governors of Texas, is one of my favorites. I was reminded of it recently as I drove past his statue off I-45 near Huntsville, and it got me thinking about what's at stake this year.
I’ve always believed that courage is contagious and a leap of faith only works if you take it. I’ve seen that play out time and again during my political career — first when I stepped up to save my child’s school from closure, then again when I walked out of the Texas Legislature and broke quorum to fight discriminatory redistricting schemes.
I’m bringing that same energy to my campaign for Governor of Texas. We know that Greg Abbott and his billionaire donors are ready to drag us through the mud in this campaign, but we aren’t going to let that reduce our fight.
This campaign is, most of all, about you. And about Texas. Every day, I’m guided by the leaders that have come before us, fought hard battles, taken risks, and won.
This campaign is about doing what’s right — for Texas, our families, our future. I know we’ll win this together.
**[I need you with me. If you’re ready to do right and risk the consequences, make a $5 contribution to support us before the critical end-of-month deadline.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260129_1_eom2.DLfmWF&refcode=em20260129-495&amount=5&t=1&akid=495%2E299639%2EaGrV1e)**

California has millions of illegal immigrants, more than any state by a mile.

Gavin Newsom gives them access to taxpayer programs paid by and intended for Californians.

He bans local law enforcement from cooperating with ICE. In Riverside County, my deputies and I are forbidden from assisting the federal government to identify violent illegals who are in our prisons.

And he likens federal immigration officials to Nazis. This only fuels the rage and chaos that we're seeing in Minneapolis. **It riles people up.**

When I am Governor, all of this will change.

_On Day 1, I will announce that the State of California will cooperate with the federal government in identifying and deporting violent illegal aliens. And I will free local officials to work with ICE if they so wish._

subject: I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MINNESOTANS FOR KLOBUCHAR**
body:
To accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support.

| | |
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4600?t=1&akid=7169%2E400544%2E9Lw5of)
Hi there —
I wanted you to be one of the first to hear the news: I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota.**This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other.**
**[I’m going to tell you why in a moment. But first: Will you help us get off to a strong start by splitting a donation between Deb Haaland's campaign and mine?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4600?t=2&akid=7169%2E400544%2E9Lw5of)**
I’m not going to sugarcoat it — Minnesota has been through a lot.
The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. Three thousand ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America’s heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will.
**These moments call for grit and resilience.** I’ve learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up.
And grit? I learned that from my family. I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1,500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn’t be where I am today without them.
**These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state.
I led our state’s biggest prosecutors’ office for eight years, and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law.
**I will do my job without fear or favor. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful. That’s what I did as prosecutor. That’s what I did as senator. And that’s what I will do as your governor.**
I believe we must stand up for what’s right. And fix what’s wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love.
And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer, and builder.
_But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support._
**This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change.**
[**So please: Will you support my campaign for governor with a donation today? Your contribution will be split with Deb Haaland for Governor.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/4600?t=3&akid=7169%2E400544%2E9Lw5of)
**I like my job in the Senate. But I love our state more than any job.** I love the people of Minnesota. And Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor.
Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us.
To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do — and that’s why I’m asking you to join us.

Amy

body:
Here at Forward, we hear you. We understand. Like we do, many of you look out on the current American political system and see something unrecognizable that doesn't make sense.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
Here at Forward, we hear you. We understand. Like we do, many of you look out on the current American political system and see something unrecognizable that doesn't make sense. Most of us hold ourselves to a high standard when it comes to the way we treat other people. In our homes, we teach our children not to argue and to learn to work together. In our jobs, we see clearly the value of compromise. These are not just American values; they are human values. And yet... When we step out of our close relationships, our homes, and our jobs, the contrast of our daily experiences with the realities of modern two-party politics is stark. Ours is a system where standards of treatment sometimes aren't apparent at all, where arguing and fabricated animosity are all-too-often rewarded, and where unwillingness to compromise may well win elections. The incentives are wrong. Tragedies like the one we witnessed in Minnesota happen. It makes you feel anxious; many of you tell us you're scared. We understand; we feel it too. And it motivates us. The same values you (and we) instill in our children are the values that should be foundational to our political system. A system that hears you and responds to you. A system driven to solve the problems our communities face. A system of values that cares. This is the system we are working to build. And with your support, we will build it. We hope you like this edition of our weekly Fast Forward. It's a window into the system that will be. Starting with... We mentioned Minnesota above. This is one of those failures of the system. In case you missed our statement, here it is. Read it, and then we'll get into what we're going to do to change this system. **Forward this to your friends, family, coworkers - helps us introduce them to Forward and what we are trying to build. We would also love it if you could invite them to one of our upcoming events listed below.**
---
---
---
So back to changing the system... We are excited about the huge, warm reception that the first episode of our newly announced podcast received! Since we're on a roll with these announcements, we have another one: We have rebranded our podcast and settled on a final name: The Forward Party Podcast. This is more descriptive and searchable and better captures the breadth of content and ideas we will be bringing to you over the coming months. Thank you for all the feedback! Now on to even more exciting things: The next episode of The Forward Party Podcast is now live! In this second episode, hosts Lindsey Drath, Gov. Christine Todd Whitman, and Lt. Gov. Kerry Healey explore a shared question shaping American civic life right now: How do we rebuild trust, restore dialogue, and lead without falling into partisan traps? The conversation brings together two distinct voices who approach that challenge from different angles, yet land on strikingly similar conclusions about leadership, speech, and responsibility. First to join them in the discussion is journalist and author Rikki Schlott, a columnist for the _New York Post_ and co-author of _The Canceling of the American Mind_. Drawing from her reporting and personal experience as a Gen Z writer navigating today’s campus climate, Rikki offers a candid look at how free speech debates, social media incentives, and institutional failures are shaping young people’s political identities. The episode then turns to Minnesota, where Mike Newcome, a Forward Party candidate for governor, joins the conversation. Mike brings a practical lens shaped by decades as a business leader and his current campaign. We hope you enjoy! Don't forget to let us know what you think. _**Click the image below to watch.**_ [](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=c1vIqT8LaeJ1yAWpG61iLkjwC2IAb4ey-sZcQKA6X4PQ5UeXv3Jp46Dbi4GtIdapqiVa8VZtM2YWBedm-E6WrA&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=1 "The Forward Party Podcast EP2 - Campus Free Speech and MN
Politics Rikki Schlott & Mike Newcome") ICYMI: [The Forward Party Podcast - Behind the Scenes reel](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=c1vIqT8LaeJ1yAWpG61iLmOf5wuwiOxk0xpqK0xdewU&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=2)

### [A third-party senator, a ‘teacher of the year’ and an ‘ordinary citizen.’ Meet Utah’s new lawmakers](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=rtTPSgvEp6UWncw5WXVsjEO-pY6qh4f5kKjxA9KAY7ht4Hiv8KOgqB1ItL_SwTMmFi2mTc4uABkKjT78fv052Vfz4S8df3YJG30VDJHJAuuxN6U1AUa9Ga8AJy37Tgzk&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=3)
_Sen. Emily Buss from Utah’s Forward party, Democratic Rep. John Arthur and Republican Rep. Leah Hansen are preparing to cast their first votes in a general session._
### [Texas Forward Party to Host First State Convention, Back Independent Slate for 2026](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=AqY7VoEUzHlAVH9yJtSeP4JMvJIHI9yhkmeGPLUbB3duH-_We_EwQ0rSp7Tw8dAUigaE9sRDr0_sZuqq97NT3heogQ_O90PofDww0-KsNeZESbvydIQQi_CiclqXDcL4jPmxCHMp32FjJs_sA4l5fu9RBwUZ3N5QA3hxzJz1Cgg&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=4)
_The Texas Forward Party will host its inaugural state convention in Austin this spring, where members will select leadership and set organizing priorities for the year ahead. The party is also seeking ballot access and backing a slate of independent candidates for the 2026 general election._
### [We can open Arizona elections to true choice](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=UeDLqzdowGDpJNWAIB-bbGvCaP-2oOPYk9LqHXFp3tM&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=5)
_For too long, Arizona’s independent voters and the civic and community leaders who would most represent their concerns have been effectively boxed out of governing. More than a third of Arizona’s voters are registered as independents, yet the rules make it drastically harder for independent candidates to compete. According to the 2024 signature requirements on the Secretary of State’s website, it takes between 6,000-7,000 signatures for a Republican or Democrat to get on the statewide ballot, but nearly 43,000 signatures for an independent. That barrier alone shuts out countless community leaders whose ideas don’t fit neatly into the rigid platforms of the Republican and Democratic parties. Yet, a simple solution to level that playing field has ignited a firestorm of controversy._

### [OPEN PRIMARIES: Independents are Surging...and independent Veterans are Spoiling for a Fight](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=1bglchNhV5n7qaCqsDLY9R9iQmUTkU4fqZOl-Ju-qOdwSKbpzbLlNpbGVp4ASuLhHfyGaDZnt11ccD4pPodhDvA40sJuHavDdPioiewHBwg&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=6)
America’s veterans still command much credibility across divides. Can independent veterans help lead the way to something new? For our first Primary Buzz of 2026, we’re introducing you to leaders on the front lines of this emerging conversation.
### [NY Monthly Virtual Town Hall](https://home.forwardparty.com/seadler/ny_monthly_virtual_town_hall_20251111_20260203?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=7)
Each month, New York Forwardists across the state meet on Google Meets to hear from a partner organization, a potential endorsed candidate, or to discuss a relevant topic. Open discussion follows. E-mail Erik to join: maverikc@gmail.com!
### [NY Forward Monthly Happy Hour](https://home.forwardparty.com/seadler/ny_forward_monthly_happy_hour_20260210?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=8)
Come join us on the second Tuesday of each month as New York Forwardists gather in Midtown Manhattan to chat politics and hang out casually. All are welcome!
### [National Volunteer Call](https://home.forwardparty.com/national_volunteer_call_20260210?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=9)
Please join our head of volunteer engagement, Carrie Anne, for a 30-minute rundown of all things Forward Party! Meet other volunteers, hear what's happening in the committees and other states, and stay abreast of party news. This call is for any level of volunteer in any state, and is a great starting point if this is your first time getting involved! Zoom meeting link will be sent after you RSVP.
### [The Power of Your Story](https://home.forwardparty.com/fwdwc_presents_power_of_your_story?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=ff_87a&n=10)
This event is a practical, introductory session designed for those who are curious about running for office, actively running, or supporting Forward-aligned candidates. The event will feature **Lauren Pinkston** , an independent candidate for Governor of Tennessee, who will share how she is using her personal story as a core part of her digital campaign and how candidates at any level can apply those strategies in their own races. Hosts **Caroline Anderson** and moderator **Kayla Sullivan** will bring their firsthand campaign experience to the conversation, highlighting key lessons learned, offering guidance for navigating a run for office, and discussing how campaign teams can effectively elevate a candidate’s story through digital media to build authentic connections with voters.

****And to report it.** This is how **prevention becomes possible**. Because one informed employee and one brave phone call can save a life.**Here's the truth most people don 't know.**The majority of trafficking in America happens in hotels and motels.And it spikes around large sports events, conventions and concerts - anywhere demand increases. **There 's more you should know. **

* Human trafficking is the second-largest criminal enterprise in the world.
* **In the United States alone, 9 out of 10 missing children are trafficked.**
* If a child is not found within 48 hours, the risk of trafficking skyrockets.
* The average age of a trafficked child is 12 to 14 years old.

name: Karen Hamilton
subject: VA LEGISLATIVE UPDATE!
body:
---
|
---
| |
---
| VIRGINIA IS FOR PATRIOTS!
---
|
---
|
---
|
---
| Patriots, Greetings from Richmond! I hope you are all weathering these extreme temperatures and staying warm! There seems to be more cold air and possible snow on the way so I will keep you updated if there are any alerts regarding electricity outages in the district.
---
|
---

Speaking of historic storms, House Democrats unleashed a major one on us this week, rushing through legislation that will authorize a vote on a Constitutional amendment that would let them gerrymander our Congressional delegation. Their goal is to send as many as 10 Democratic members to Congress in a state that splits about down the middle most years. That’s not right. What makes it worse is how dishonest they’re being about it, in addition to being sneaky. Rather than hold multiple hearings on the bill, they gave everyone, legislators and the public alike, 30 minutes notice, and in an odd committee. No public comment, no chance for those opposed to give their input. The most deceptive part is how they plan to describe the amendment on your ballot in April: "Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to allow the General Assembly to temporarily adopt new congressional districts to restore fairness in the upcoming elections, while ensuring Virginia's standard redistricting process resumes for all future redistricting after the 2030 census?" Well, who could be against ‘fairness’? In all seriousness, we’re working hard to force them to change this to something more realistic, or in the worst case, ensure that Virginians know just what this thing is going to do if it passes--an uphill battle!
However, on Tuesday, we received a glimmer of hope! A circuit court judge in Tazewell County granted an injunction on the gerrymandering amendment. He concluded that the processes taken by the Democrats were in violation of current law. The democrats will appeal this and it may end up at the Supreme Court of Virginia. I'll keep you posted. Either way, the power is in your hands now.Remember, we can stop this power grab and the other amendments, but only if YOU get to the polls and vote.You can visit this [website](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/f8PmBZ_Zz/c?w=TuTUqvMZ3pH4P0tTmxpHRZMheYkDo5ErPJ9EtBBSsEI.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly92b3RlLmVsZWN0aW9ucy52aXJnaW5pYS5nb3YvVm90ZXJJbmZvcm1hdGlvbiIsInIiOiIiLCJtIjoibWFpbCIsImMiOiI0NDI4ODkzMy1lNGNjLTRmMTItOGYzZS02ZjQ1ZjM3NjIxZjQifQ) to join the permanent absentee voter list.
It's been a busy week for me personally, as I've presented 6 bills in subcommittees. I would thank those who made an effort to testify in support of them, at a short notice and in inclement weather! Chairman of Madison Co. Board of Supervisors--Jim Jewett,Member of the Madison Planning Commission--Jim Smith, Chairman of Culpeper Co. Board of Supervisors--Tom UnderwoodPresident of Virginia Medical Freedom Alliance--Dr. Sheila FurreyFounder of We Are The Resistance--Anne Craft Taydus Thank you! Your expert testimony and efforts were greatly appreciated!! Unfortunately only one of my bills so far has made it to the next step--full committee. This particular bill (HB 538) is an important one that allows child sex abuse victims to seek justice, and facilitates a more accurate list of the sex offender registry in Virginia. I am praying that this will be a bi-partisan bill that goes through. I've also gotten hundreds of emails from Virginians upset about the all out Democrat assault on our right to keep and bear arms.Keep the pressure on legislators! I want to assure you that I will oppose all of these unconstitutional restrictions, but prepare for most of them to pass along party lines. Plan accordingly and I recommend contacting your Sheriff to encourage them to stand strong in their oath to the Constitution. Also, you may sign up in advance to oppose them online when they are in Public Safety Committee this FRIDAY at 8am:link here
In other news, Democrats have introduced around 50 bills that either increase your taxes or impose fees of various kinds, making your daily lives more expensive....so much for all that "affordability" talk. Virginians who supported the Democrat agenda are going to develop a rough case of "buyer's remorse" if these bills that tax a variety of things-- from Amazon deliveries and gym memberships to electric leaf blowers and home repairs--go through. Lastly, please keep Virginia and those in government in your prayers. There are many cordial people here on the other side of the aisle, and some that claim a faith in God, but there is a darkness in the minds of those who give more rights to a murderer and rapist than a full term, healthy unborn baby.It's a disturbing and grievous thing to witness such evil legislation pass in Virginia. Once again, thank you for giving me the privilege of representing you in Richmond. As always, if I or my staff may be of assistance to you in any way, please don't hesitate to contact me. DelKHamilton@house.virginia.gov(804) 698-1062 Delegate Karen F. Hamilton

clean_body: | | | | VIRGINIA IS FOR PATRIOTS! | | | | Patriots, Greetings from Richmond! I hope you are all weathering these extreme temperatures and staying warm! There seems to be more cold air and possible snow on the way so I will keep you updated if there are any alerts regarding electricity outages in the district. | Speaking of historic storms, House Democrats unleashed a major one on us this week, rushing through legislation that will authorize a vote on a Constitutional amendment that would let them gerrymander our Congressional delegation. Their goal is to send as many as 10 Democratic members to Congress in a state that splits about down the middle most years. That’s not right. What makes it worse is how dishonest they’re being about it, in addition to being sneaky. Rather than hold multiple hearings on the bill, they gave everyone, legislators and the public alike, 30 minutes notice, and in an odd committee. No public comment, no chance for those opposed to give their input. The most deceptive part is how they plan to describe the amendment on your ballot in April: "Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to allow the General Assembly to temporarily adopt new congressional districts to restore fairness in the upcoming elections, while ensuring Virginia's standard redistricting process resumes for all future redistricting after the 2030 census?" Well, who could be against ‘fairness’? In all seriousness, we’re working hard to force them to change this to something more realistic, or in the worst case, ensure that Virginians know just what this thing is going to do if it passes--an uphill battle! However, on Tuesday, we received a glimmer of hope! A circuit court judge in Tazewell County granted an injunction on the gerrymandering amendment. He concluded that the processes taken by the Democrats were in violation of current law. The democrats will appeal this and it may end up at the Supreme Court of Virginia. I'll keep you posted. Either way, the power is in your hands now.Remember, we can stop this power grab and the other amendments, but only if YOU get to the polls and vote.You can visit this to join the permanent absentee voter list. It's been a busy week for me personally, as I've presented 6 bills in subcommittees. I would thank those who made an effort to testify in support of them, at a short notice and in inclement weather! Chairman of Madison Co. Board of Supervisors--Jim Jewett,Member of the Madison Planning Commission--Jim Smith, Chairman of Culpeper Co. Board of Supervisors--Tom UnderwoodPresident of Virginia Medical Freedom Alliance--Dr. Sheila FurreyFounder of We Are The Resistance--Anne Craft Taydus Thank you! Your expert testimony and efforts were greatly appreciated!! Unfortunately only one of my bills so far has made it to the next step--full committee. This particular bill (HB 538) is an important one that allows child sex abuse victims to seek justice, and facilitates a more accurate list of the sex offender registry in Virginia. I am praying that this will be a bi-partisan bill that goes through. I've also gotten hundreds of emails from Virginians upset about the all out Democrat assault on our right to keep and bear arms.Keep the pressure on legislators! I want to assure you that I will oppose all of these unconstitutional restrictions, but prepare for most of them to pass along party lines. Plan accordingly and I recommend contacting your Sheriff to encourage them to stand strong in their oath to the Constitution. Also, you may sign up in advance to oppose them online when they are in Public Safety Committee this FRIDAY at 8am:link here In other news, Democrats have introduced around 50 bills that either increase your taxes or impose fees of various kinds, making your daily lives more expensive....so much for all that "affordability" talk. Virginians who supported the Democrat agenda are going to develop a rough case of "buyer's remorse" if these bills that tax a variety of things-- from Amazon deliveries and gym memberships to electric leaf blowers and home repairs--go through. Lastly, please keep Virginia and those in government in your prayers. There are many cordial people here on the other side of the aisle, and some that claim a faith in God, but there is a darkness in the minds of those who give more rights to a murderer and rapist than a full term, healthy unborn baby.It's a disturbing and grievous thing to witness such evil legislation pass in Virginia. Once again, thank you for giving me the privilege of representing you in Richmond. As always, if I or my staff may be of assistance to you in any way, please don't hesitate to contact me. DelKHamilton@house.virginia.gov(804) 698-1062 Delegate Karen F. subject: Dying state? People are fleeing New Mexico
body:

| | | | | |
They're leaving New Mexico. And they're not coming back. Census just confirmed it: we're one of only FIVE states losing population. More people dying than being born. [Ranked dead last to raise a family.](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=8daeaeba23&e=567664f14c)

| |
**📉 NEW MEXICO IS SHRINKING — AND SANTA FE DOESN'T CARE**
The census numbers are brutal. We break down exactly how bad it's gotten — and why the two bills moving through the legislature right now would accelerate the collapse.
One would gut school funding and Medicaid. The other violates the Constitution. House Republicans just sent a letter to the DOJ.
**Your reps need to hear from you before it's too late: nmlegis.gov**
---

---
| |
**💀 THE VIDEO THAT CHANGES EVERYTHING**
New footage just surfaced showing Alex Peretti 10 days before he was shot in Minneapolis.
What he does in this video should have landed him in handcuffs. It didn't. They let him walk.
10 days later, he showed up armed again.
We show you the moment Minnesota failed him — and why he'd be alive today if they'd enforced the law.

**📞 TRUMP AND WALZ JUST TALKED**
Nobody expected this call. Trump says they're "on a similar wavelength." Tom Homan is heading to Minnesota.
Something shifted. We break down what — and what it means.

| |
**🎬 ED NORTON WANTS YOU TO QUIT YOUR JOB**
A Hollywood millionaire called for a "national general economic strike."
Batya Ungar-Sargon said what we're all thinking. We play the clip.

**🍎 ILHAN OMAR "ATTACKED" — WITH APPLE CIDER VINEGAR**
CNN tried to connect it to "violence in Minnesota."
You have to see how they framed this.

Hundreds of thousands of households across the South are without power in freezing temperatures.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124304681/598200112/1328794144?refcode=ea.2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ms=ea.2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjJkNGNhMjQ4LTVkZmQtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=YmnLiQtP2k9Y-2jnIPFTJGa0yeByRIH7Viz_99Y8p-E=&emci=425952bd-3efd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4823105)

**I’m reaching out today because severe winter storms have blanketed the nation, pushing at least 16 states to declare states of emergency.** Hundreds of thousands of households across the South — especially in Mississippi and Tennessee — are without power in freezing temperatures. And with extremely cold conditions expected to persist into early February, even short-term outages can quickly become life-threatening. Many Southern communities do not have the infrastructure to treat snow and ice at scale. Roads become impassable. Power outages can last days (_even up to ten!_). And as we know, it’s the most vulnerable who pay the highest price: elders, families already facing food or housing insecurity, rural communities with limited access to services, and people who rely on electricity for medical equipment or heat. This is where an organization I truly admire, **REBUILD** , steps in. REBUILD.US is working closely with hundreds of organizations to get resources where they’re needed most, including in Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, North and South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Virginia. That looks like warm clothing, generators, non-perishable food, and simple but lifesaving support like gift cards that allow people to meet their most urgent needs with dignity. **I believe deeply in the power, and the responsibility, of community. It’s a huge reason why I founded JanePAC. We’ve built a movement of people like you who organize not only to elect better leaders — though that work is essential — but to show up for one another when crisis hits.** **[If you’re able, I hope you’ll consider making a contribution today to support REBUILD’s frontline relief work. Your support helps ensure that communities facing the worst of these storms are not left to face them alone.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124304682/598200113/823200407?_gl=1*10nvulv*_gcl_au*MTc1NjcwMjY4My4xNzY5MTk5MTQy&refcode=ea.2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ms=ea.2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjJkNGNhMjQ4LTVkZmQtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=YmnLiQtP2k9Y-2jnIPFTJGa0yeByRIH7Viz_99Y8p-E=&emci=425952bd-3efd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4823105)** With gratitude, Jane [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124304683/598200114/823200407?_gl=1*10nvulv*_gcl_au*MTc1NjcwMjY4My4xNzY5MTk5MTQy&refcode=ea.2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ms=ea.2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjJkNGNhMjQ4LTVkZmQtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=YmnLiQtP2k9Y-2jnIPFTJGa0yeByRIH7Viz_99Y8p-E=&emci=425952bd-3efd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=2d4ca248-5dfd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4823105)

body:
Our grassroots team must be ready to jump into action in several states as soon as this ruling comes down.
|
---

Peter,
You want to know what’s keeping us all up at night?
**"If the [Supreme Court] invalidates Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the decision could unleash chaos at every level of government. Multiple states ... are already plotting new rounds of redistricting that could severely undermine the political representation of voters of color."**
That assessment from NYU Law Professor Kareem Crayton sums up just how much is at stake in the upcoming Supreme Court decision _Louisiana v. Callais_. Not only could a half century of progress on equal representation be wiped away, but it could immediately set off a new, devastating round of mid-decade redistricting in an attempt to stack the deck before the midterms on the backs of communities of color across the country.
Our grassroots team must be ready to jump into action in several states to respond on the ground as soon as this ruling comes down, which could happen any day now.

"If the [Supreme Court] invalidates Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, the decision could unleash chaos at every level of government. Multiple states ... are already plotting new rounds of redistricting that could severely undermine the political representation of voters of color." That assessment from NYU Law Professor Kareem Crayton sums up just how much is at stake in the upcoming Supreme Court decision Louisiana v. Callais. Not only could a half century of progress on equal representation be wiped away, but it could immediately set off a new, devastating round of mid-decade redistricting in an attempt to stack the deck before the midterms on the backs of communities of color across the country. body:
We have two days — and a powerful opportunity — to protect fair elections in Virginia.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/131?refcode=em20260129-90&t=1&akid=90%2E12592%2EiTdale)
Hi,
Right now, we’re preparing to fully launch our voter education program across the Commonwealth. But to launch at the scale we need to get the word out to every Virginian, [**we need to raise $50,000 by midnight on January 31st. Can you chip in today to help us reach our goal?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/300?t=2&akid=90%2E12592%2EiTdale)
The opening days of a campaign shape _everything_ that comes next. How fast we move, how effectively we reach voters, and whether we’re positioned to succeed in the fight ahead are all determined by how we start. We have a critical opportunity to build early momentum — **and we have just two days left to do it.**
Our goal is simple: make sure Virginians understand what this amendment does, how it safeguards fair representation, and why voting **YES** matters _before_ they cast their ballots.
MAGA Republicans already know this amendment threatens their political advantage. That’s why we expect a sustained effort to blur facts in the months ahead.

name: Carmela Conroy
subject: Crushing freedom to dissent
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CONROY FOR CONGRESS
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=bb686be293&e=a7b299e420)
| | | | | |
Peter,

**What we are witnessing in Minnesota and across the country should alarm every one of us who believes in the rule of law, human dignity, and civil rights.**

The federal government has militarized immigration enforcement to terrorize communities, brutalize families, and kill American citizens. ICE and other armed agents are being diverted from securing the border and running prisons, deployed as partisan paramilitary forces against parts of the country where Democrats are in office - the kind of authoritarian abuse I witnessed firsthand while serving as a Foreign Service Officer overseas.

**We all deserve better.**

Moments like this demand moral clarity and leadership. Yet our freshman representative is doing the opposite: voting to provide blank-check funding to the Department of Homeland Security with no accountability or plan to prevent further violence, slandering judges who rule against DHS abuse of power, and criticizing Washington state’s sanctuary laws that protect our neighbors and ensure due process.

We can do better - we’ve seen what that looks like. Washington Senators Patty Murray and Maria Cantwell are leading the fight in the Senate for transparency, dignity, and real guardrails on ICE. **We deserve that same kind of leadership here in Eastern Washington.**

I’ll be clear: If Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem does not resign, the House must impeach her. Congress must also exercise oversight and defund agencies that endanger citizens, law-abiding immigrants, and visitors. The executive branch must redirect ICE and other border enforcement agents to borders and ports - and if it does not, Congress must act.

**I know so many are feeling anger, fear, and pain. Images from Minneapolis remind me of historic images from the Civil Rights movement of the 1960s that sparked anger, shame - and good trouble. But I also am hearing this: people are ready to take action.**

If you’re ready to help make our freshman representative’s first term his last, I invite you to join our campaign as a volunteer today. [**Sign up here, and we’ll be in touch soon with ways you can make a difference right here at home.**](https://conroy4congress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc047fbc65030d4c4bcc44d19&id=55d2028ab7&e=a7b299e420) **And please, send this message to three neighbors so they can join the movement too.**

Most of all, my team and I are always listening. Whether you’re devastated by the violence of this administration or worried about issues here at home, you’re welcome to hit reply and share your thoughts.

I look forward to hearing from you - and I’ll be in touch soon with more updates.

In solidarity,

Carmela Conroy

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260129em-fbi [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260129em-fbi]
Yesterday, at the direction of Donald Trump’s FBI, agents raided Fulton County election facilities connected to the 2020 election — an election that has already been audited, reviewed, investigated, and certified.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260129em-fbi [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260129em-fbi]
There is no new evidence of fraud. There never has been. But the same false claims are still being recycled, even after they’ve been disproven over and over again.
As a scientist, I’m trained to follow the data. When the data is wrong, you correct it. When the facts don’t support a claim, you move on.
What’s happening instead is the opposite. People in power are continuing to undermine trust in our elections because it benefits them politically — even when it puts real Georgians in danger.
We’ve already seen what those lies lead to: Election workers were targeted, families were threatened, and our Capitol was attacked by a conspiratorial mob.
That should have been the end of it. Instead, years later, the same story is being dragged back into the spotlight for political gain.
That’s one of the reasons I decided to run for Congress. I’ve spent my time in the legislature calling out false data, exposing misinformation, and forcing corrections when leaders tried to bend the truth. Whether it was COVID reporting, attacks on public education, or junk science being used to justify extreme laws — I didn’t stay quiet. And I’m not going to start now.
Georgia needs leaders who understand the facts, tell the truth, and are willing to call out misinformation. But I need your help to win this race, so I’m asking you personally to chip in today and help us build the strongest grassroots campaign possible. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260129em-fbi]

The last time the Trump administration attacked the census, the fair maps movement won — and we must win again.
| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124306960/598207225/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNmYmI2YzBkLTYyZmQtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=-l7lDDMVRZ88S8rtmsd8LnKa95_03eCkekG6sg18ado=&emci=92afae25-30fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=cfbb6c0d-62fd-f011-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=8431045)
---

Peter, fair elections depend on fair maps, which require an accurate population count. That’s why we are fighting back against Trump and MAGA attempts to undermine a critical part of the equation: the U.S. Census. Trump and his anti-democracy allies are levying multiple attacks on the 2030 Census:
* One federal lawsuit demands that the Census Bureau not count undocumented people in determining redistricting congressional districts.

* Another lawsuit wants to end methods that are used to protect participants’ privacy and ensure that people in group-living facilities are counted — and even retroactively revise past figures.

* Meanwhile, the administration disbanded advisory commissions — groups of experts that had ensured the census was conducted based on the best research.

We’re incredibly concerned about the potential implementation of these wildly unconstitutional actions and the impact they could have on the shape of American democracy. [**When they tried to undermine the census during the first Trump administration, the fair maps movement fought back hard — and prevailed. Will you make a donation to support the NDRC’s efforts to protect democracy from every effort to undermine it?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124306961/598207226/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_2030Census_email_20260129-NDRC-Tier1-2030Census_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260129-NDRC-Tier1-2030Census_&utm_campaign=2030Census&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNmYmI2YzBkLTYyZmQtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=-l7lDDMVRZ88S8rtmsd8LnKa95_03eCkekG6sg18ado=) The Trump administration isn’t being coy about why it’s hoping to meddle with the census. They want to handpick the people who get to have a voice in this country — just like they’re seeking to do with mid-decade map redraws. But the census is the people’s data — created for the people, by the people, to represent the people. And the Constitution is crystal clear about who gets counted. Without an accurate count of the people, fair representation in the House of Representatives and allocations for state funding will be in jeopardy. **We must stop this cynical, unconstitutional power grab.** **The NDRC is fighting back on behalf of democracy on multiple fronts at once.[Your support will make an urgently needed impact to defend free elections, fair maps, and a truly representative democracy.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124306962/598207227/1128139581?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_2030Census_email_20260129-NDRC-Tier1-2030Census_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260129-NDRC-Tier1-2030Census_&utm_campaign=2030Census&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImNmYmI2YzBkLTYyZmQtZjAxMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=-l7lDDMVRZ88S8rtmsd8LnKa95_03eCkekG6sg18ado=)** Thank you for strengthening our fight, Marina Jenkins

**I’m calling for the impeachment of Kristi Noem as secretary of homeland security.**

Over the last year, Secretary Noem’s leadership has been reckless, chaotic, and corrupt. Under her purview, our country is less safe. It’s time for accountability.

State Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland) with U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.)
Maine Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland), whose political ascent as one of the first Somali-Americans in the Maine Legislature once made national headlines, announced Thursday that she will not seek reelection to the Maine House.
Dhalac blamed her exit on a political climate she described as "increasingly hostile and unsafe" and cited "persistent racism" and harassment, though she was not able to provide any examples of such harassment.
Throughout her career, Dhalac has been unapologetic about placing Somalia first. Despite serving the people of South Portland, she has frequently made statements that suggest a different set of loyalties.
"We Somalis living outside of Somalia must always prioritize our country, Somalia," Dhalac stated in a previously published video.

## Gateway Community Services and the Migrant-Industrial Complex
Gateway's house of cards began to collapse largely due to the investigative work of the Maine Wire and The Robinson Report, which first exposed the murky intersection of taxpayer-funded NGOs and Democratic political activism.
Investigations into DHHS audit records and no-bid contract documents revealed that Gateway, under the leadership of Ali and Dhalac, billed MaineCare -- the state's version of Medicaid -- for approximately $28.8 million between 2019 and 2024. During the same time, the agency faced three DHHS audits which all found serious record-keeping lapses with Gateway's reimbursement requests.
Even more staggering was the flow of no-bid contracts from state agencies. Although DHHS audits had flagged issues with Gateway's finances, the Mills Administration continued to pump federal dollars into the organization through opaque no-bid contracts, including contracts that funded activities indiscernible from Democratic electioneering.
Despite a lack of interest from Maine's newspapers and AG Frey's decision to take a pass on investigating Gateway, national attention prompted both federal law enforcement and congressional investigators to take a closer look at Gateway, Ali, and Dhalac.
The legal pressure reached a fever pitch on Dec. 30, when more than a dozen Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents were seen descending on Gateway's Lewiston offices at 124 Canal St.

HSI officials confirmed they are conducting audits to protect the country from fraud and ensure businesses employ legal workers, an investigation that has targeted several Somali-linked nonprofits in the region.
This raid followed a high-profile request from House Oversight Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.), who demanded banking records and Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) from the U.S. Treasury Department for both Ali and Dhalac. ## Gateway & the Community Organizing Alliance
Gateway was more than just a migrant service provider; it was a political machine.
Almost immediately after receiving no-bid contracts to fund "[Community Health Outreach Workers](https://substack.com/redirect/ab518d4f-9d17-45fe-8203-b041ed5a3d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," Ali and top [Gateway](https://substack.com/redirect/ab518d4f-9d17-45fe-8203-b041ed5a3d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) employees, Safiya Khalid and Mohamed Khalid, formed the [Community Organizing Alliance (COA)](https://substack.com/redirect/ab518d4f-9d17-45fe-8203-b041ed5a3d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The [COA](https://substack.com/redirect/ab518d4f-9d17-45fe-8203-b041ed5a3d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) board had top migrant NGO leaders, including Ali himself and Fatuma Hussein, but also Maine Democrat bigwigs like lobbyist B.J. McCollister, Maureen Drouin from Maine Conservation Voters, and abortion activist Joanne D'Arcangelo.
Since scandal enveloped Gateway, whoever controls the [COA](https://substack.com/redirect/ab518d4f-9d17-45fe-8203-b041ed5a3d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) website has deleted the page listing its board members, and both Safiya and Mohamed Khalid have updated their LinkedIn profiles to indicate that they no longer work at [COA](https://substack.com/redirect/ab518d4f-9d17-45fe-8203-b041ed5a3d0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which was headquartered at the Gateway offices in Lewiston.
According to a disclosure that once appeared on its website, the COA had a fiscal sponsorship from the left-wing Maine People's Alliance and its 501(c)3 arm, the Maine People's Resource Center.
The COA, in its own words, was dedicated to voter turnout in migrant communities and operated out of Gateway's own offices.
In the lead-up to Mills' 2022 reelection campaign, while taxpayer money continued to flow into Gateway's accounts through federal COVID-19 relief and no-bid contracts, COA was campaigning for Mills and other Democrats using the same office and the same staff.
In fact, the no-bid contracts Gateway received specifically required the agency to go door-to-door in migrant communities signing migrants up for Medicaid and food stamps, buying them household supplies, and keeping a database on all contacts. The contract allowed Gateway to keep that database for its own purposes, meaning Gateway and COA were effectively paid with taxpayer dollars to hand out free healthcare, free food, and free household supplies while building a database of voters with a high propensity to vote for Democrats.

Friends,
I just joined a coalition of 21 state attorneys general to condemn the Trump administration’s latest attempt to exploit the situation in Minnesota.
They’re pressuring state officials to illegally turn over sensitive resident data and dismantle long-standing public safety policies.
These actions are unprecedented. They’re deeply troubling, and the bottom line is that they amount to coercion. Sign on to our petition today if you agree the DOJ is violating Minnesota’s state sovereignty. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/ZAPf0zeSskCEEhbCuQ6KRA2]
Let’s get into exactly what happened:
Over the weekend, Pam Bondi’s DOJ demanded a series of concessions in exchange for withdrawing federal immigration enforcement agents from the state.
Those demands included turning over private Medicaid and SNAP data, granting access to voter information, and rolling back critical public safety protections.
That is not law enforcement — it’s extortion.
These demands trample on state sovereignty, violate individual privacy, and attempt to sidestep court orders blocking nearly identical federal data grabs.
Don’t forget: this administration already ran these plays in California and in other states, and when we fought back, judges across the country blocked their illegal actions.
Now, the U.S. Department of Justice is now trying to force outcomes it couldn’t achieve legally — while exploiting a tragic situation to do it.
Ultimately, this isn’t just about Minnesota. It’s about whether states are allowed to govern ourselves. It’s about whether families can trust that their personal data won’t be weaponized by the federal government. And it’s about whether the rule of law still matters.
Add your name if you agree: The U.S. DOJ’s demand for illegal data is a violation of Minnesota’s right to govern themselves. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/ZAPf0zeSskCEEhbCuQ6KRA2]
ADD YOUR NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/ZAPf0zeSskCEEhbCuQ6KRA2]
I stand firmly with Minnesota and with attorneys general across the country against these illegal threats.
We will continue to defend state sovereignty, protect people’s privacy, and push back against federal overreach wherever it appears.
In solidarity,
Rob

Attorney General of California

I'm not going to sugarcoat it — Minnesota has been through a lot.

The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. 3,000 ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America's heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will.

**These moments call for grit and resilience.** I've learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up.

And grit? I learned that from my family. I'm the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1,500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn't be where I am today without them.

**These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state.

I led our state's biggest prosecutors' office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law.

**I will do my job without fear or favor. I've never shied away from taking on the powerful. That's what I did as prosecutor. That's what I did as senator. And that's what I will do as your governor.**

I believe we must stand up for what's right. And fix what's wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable health care. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love.

And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder.

_But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support. _

**This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change.**

The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. 3,000 ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America's heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will. These moments call for grit and resilience. I've learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up. And grit? I learned that from my family. I'm the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1,500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn't be where I am today without them. These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration. But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state. I led our state's biggest prosecutors' office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law. I will do my job without fear or favor. I've never shied away from taking on the powerful. That's what I did as prosecutor. That's what I did as senator. And that's what I will do as your governor. * * *
Something important just happened in Washington, D.C. -- and the reaction to it tells you almost everything you need to know about where American politics actually is right now.
Every Senate Democrat just voted to block a Department of Homeland Security funding package because it included money for ICE and CBP without meaningful reforms following the murder of Alex Pretti this weekend. The vote failed 45-55\. Funding runs out this week. A partial government shutdown is looking more and more likely.
Immediately, the panic set in.
You can feel it coming from the White House, from Republican leadership, from the usual chorus of pundits who rush in anytime Democrats show the slightest willingness to use power effectively. The same voices always show up in moments like this. The ones who say Democrats need to be "responsible," need to "de-escalate," need to "govern like adults." The ones who treat the possibility of any shutdown like a moral failing instead of what it actually is: leverage.
Here's the part people shouldn't miss: this wasn't a handful of protest votes. This wasn't some fringe faction making noise. Every single Senate Democrat -- including John Fetterman and seven Republican senators -- said no.
And that didn't happen in a vacuum. It happened after Pretti's murder. After intense public outcry. After people like you and me called our representatives nonstop, took to the streets, and made our voices heard. And after seven House Democrats voted for this same package the week before -- and caught hell for it.
The politics shifted fast -- and the Senate responded. They did their job.
Not because it was politically convenient, although I would argue it is. Not simple because it polls well. But because at some point, refusing to fund broken and corrupt systems without accountability has to mean something.
You don't have to agree with every tactic to understand that something important shifted here. Today, Democrats didn't blink first.
* * *

Just $8/month makes a huge difference:](https://substack.com/redirect/89990f51-115e-4c85-878b-628122a8db72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
And that matters, because it speaks directly to the anxiety a lot of Democrats are feeling right now -- anxiety that I think is completely rational.
If you're paying attention, you're not just worried about the next election. You're worried about whether this party is even capable of holding power long enough to actually change anything. You're looking at a system that feels rigged: a rigged Supreme Court loaded with Republican operatives instead of jurists, a Congress that's wildly malapportioned, and a media ecosystem that rewards bad faith and outrage porn.
Meanwhile, Republicans don't want to build anything. They want stasis or destruction -- both of which are easier than governing. They benefit from a system that lets them punch above their weight, and they play it ruthlessly. Gerrymandering. Court-packing in all but name. Weaponized outrage. No apologies.
So when people ask me, "How are we not just completely screwed?" -- I get it. I really do.
But here's the pivot point almost every one of these conversations misses.
The biggest problem Democrats have isn't that the odds are stacked against us. It's what we do after we win.
Because here's the uncomfortable truth: Democrats actually know how to win elections. We're pretty good at it -- I'd argue we should have lost more in 2024, but we ran better campaigns and candidates than the Republicans did and were running against terrible headwinds (Biden and the economy.)
When the stakes are clear and the contrast is sharp, we win, and our policies are vastly better than the alternative IMHO. Remember: Trump is underwater on nearly every major issue and is more unpopular now than Biden ever was at this point in his term.
Electorates aren't static. They never have been. Bill Clinton won Louisiana. Barack Obama won Iowa, Indiana, Florida, and North Carolina. States that feel impossible today won't feel impossible forever -- especially in an economy where 60 percent of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck and we'll have new nominees for president from both political parties in 2028.
Yes, the map is hard. Yes, the rules are rigged. But that's not what keeps me up at night.
What keeps me up at night is this: what happens when Democrats actually get power again?
Too often, the answer from Democratic strategists (of which, I am one) is predictable. Restore the norms. Move slowly. Don't scare donors. Don't upset the editorial boards. Don't look "too political" while holding political power.
That mindset is a losing governing strategy in an asymmetric fight.
Republicans understand power. They use it like they might never get it again -- because sometimes they don't. They move fast. They stack courts. They rewrite rules. They create outcomes that are hard to reverse.
Democrats, by contrast, don't treat power like something to wield -- they treat it like something that needs to be justified. Like it's inherently temporary. Like using it too aggressively might somehow disqualify them from holding it at all.
That's why this DHS funding vote matters.
Not because ICE is the whole fight. Not because a shutdown is inherently good. But because withholding power is still power -- and today, Democrats acted like they understand that.
If Democrats want to win power back and actually keep it, governing has to look fundamentally different next time. Structural reform can't be an afterthought. It has to happen immediately. Day one, not year two. Kill the filibuster. Expand the Supreme Court. Add D.C. and Puerto Rico as states. Not because it's provocative, but because Republicans have been playing unfair for decades, and pretending otherwise is malpractice. It's time to use power the way they use power, except we'll use it to save our democracy and improve your life.
And it can't stop there. Economic populism has to be real -- and it has to be big. Not tinkering. Not pilot programs. Real material changes that let people afford housing, raise a family on one income if they choose, get sick without going broke, retire with dignity, and take a goddamn vacation every now and again. If people can't feel the difference in their daily lives, nothing else we do is going to matter.
At the same time, Democrats have to get serious about corruption in America. We cannot keep living in a country where members of Congress can trade stocks using nonpublic information, where presidents pardon their friends and family, where crypto scams flourish, and where lobbyists effectively write the laws. That means investigations. Public accountability. Consequences. Real laws with real enforcement. Not out of revenge, but because letting corruption go unpunished is how democracies rot from the inside.
And while we're at it, Democrats need to stop being afraid of the fight.
The right-wing media ecosystem is going to lose its mind no matter what we do. So stop governing like Fox News approval is attainable. Go on Fox. Go on Joe Rogan. Argue for hours. Explain the choices. Defend the outcomes. Sell the fight everywhere, all the time.
Because the one question Democrats can never allow again is this: "What have you actually done for me lately?" That question should be impossible to ask with a straight face.
That's why this moment matters. This vote isn't the whole story -- but it is a signal. It says we're done reflexively funding broken systems. It says we're willing to take political heat. It says we understand leverage. It says we're not blinking first anymore.
Hope doesn't come from pretending the odds are even. Hope comes from deciding to fight like the stakes are real -- because they are.
If Democrats win in 2026 or 2028 and go right back to cautious, technocratic, "let's not rock the boat" governance, we will lose again -- and we'll deserve it.
But if we take power with urgency, if we move fast, if we're bold, if we're annoying about our wins, if we actually help people and make it impossible to ignore -- then this moment won't be remembered as chaos.
It'll be remembered as the point where Democrats finally decided to act like they understand how to wield power effectively.
And that's how you build a future worth hoping for.

If you're paying attention, you're not just worried about the next election. You're worried about whether this party is even capable of holding power long enough to actually change anything. You're looking at a system that feels rigged: a rigged Supreme Court loaded with Republican operatives instead of jurists, a Congress that's wildly malapportioned, and a media ecosystem that rewards bad faith and outrage porn. Meanwhile, Republicans don't want to build anything. They want stasis or destruction -- both of which are easier than governing. They benefit from a system that lets them punch above their weight, and they play it ruthlessly. Gerrymandering. Court-packing in all but name. Weaponized outrage. No apologies. So when people ask me, "How are we not just completely screwed?" -- I get it. I really do. But here's the pivot point almost every one of these conversations misses. The biggest problem Democrats have isn't that the odds are stacked against us. It's what we do after we win. Because here's the uncomfortable truth: Democrats actually know how to win elections. We're pretty good at it -- I'd argue we should have lost more in 2024, but we ran better campaigns and candidates than the Republicans did and were running against terrible headwinds (Biden and the economy.) When the stakes are clear and the contrast is sharp, we win, and our policies are vastly better than the alternative IMHO. Remember: Trump is underwater on nearly every major issue and is more unpopular now than Biden ever was at this point in his term. Electorates aren't static. They never have been. Bill Clinton won Louisiana. Barack Obama won Iowa, Indiana, Florida, and North Carolina. States that feel impossible today won't feel impossible forever -- especially in an economy where 60 percent of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck and we'll have new nominees for president from both political parties in 2028. Yes, the map is hard. Yes, the rules are rigged. But that's not what keeps me up at night. What keeps me up at night is this: what happens when Democrats actually get power again? Too often, the answer from Democratic strategists (of which, I am one) is predictable. Restore the norms. Move slowly. Don't scare donors. Don't upset the editorial boards. Don't look "too political" while holding political power. That mindset is a losing governing strategy in an asymmetric fight. Republicans understand power. They use it like they might never get it again -- because sometimes they don't. They move fast. They stack courts. They rewrite rules. They create outcomes that are hard to reverse. Democrats, by contrast, don't treat power like something to wield -- they treat it like something that needs to be justified. Like it's inherently temporary. Like using it too aggressively might somehow disqualify them from holding it at all. That's why this DHS funding vote matters. Not because ICE is the whole fight. Not because a shutdown is inherently good. But because withholding power is still power -- and today, Democrats acted like they understand that. If Democrats want to win power back and actually keep it, governing has to look fundamentally different next time. Structural reform can't be an afterthought. It has to happen immediately. Day one, not year two. Kill the filibuster. Expand the Supreme Court. Add D.C. and Puerto Rico as states. Not because it's provocative, but because Republicans have been playing unfair for decades, and pretending otherwise is malpractice. It's time to use power the way they use power, except we'll use it to save our democracy and improve your life. And it can't stop there. Economic populism has to be real -- and it has to be big. Not tinkering. Not pilot programs. Real material changes that let people afford housing, raise a family on one income if they choose, get sick without going broke, retire with dignity, and take a goddamn vacation every now and again. If people can't feel the difference in their daily lives, nothing else we do is going to matter. At the same time, Democrats have to get serious about corruption in America. We cannot keep living in a country where members of Congress can trade stocks using nonpublic information, where presidents pardon their friends and family, where crypto scams flourish, and where lobbyists effectively write the laws. That means investigations. Public accountability. Consequences. Real laws with real enforcement. Not out of revenge, but because letting corruption go unpunished is how democracies rot from the inside. And while we're at it, Democrats need to stop being afraid of the fight. The right-wing media ecosystem is going to lose its mind no matter what we do. So stop governing like Fox News approval is attainable. Go on Fox. Go on Joe Rogan. Argue for hours. Explain the choices. Defend the outcomes. Sell the fight everywhere, all the time. Because the one question Democrats can never allow again is this: "What have you actually done for me lately?" That question should be impossible to ask with a straight face. That's why this moment matters. This vote isn't the whole story -- but it is a signal. It says we're done reflexively funding broken systems. It says we're willing to take political heat. It says we understand leverage. It says we're not blinking first anymore. Hope doesn't come from pretending the odds are even. Hope comes from deciding to fight like the stakes are real -- because they are. If Democrats win in 2026 or 2028 and go right back to cautious, technocratic, "let's not rock the boat" governance, we will lose again -- and we'll deserve it. But if we take power with urgency, if we move fast, if we're bold, if we're annoying about our wins, if we actually help people and make it impossible to ignore -- then this moment won't be remembered as chaos. It'll be remembered as the point where Democrats finally decided to act like they understand how to wield power effectively. And that's how you build a future worth hoping for. Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes.
