# Sen. Durbin parades fake AI shooting poster on the Senate floor, gets mocked ruthlessly
Sen. Dick Durbin (D-IL) **[brandished a large poster on the Senate floor](https://substack.com/redirect/1e16bf38-5261-48e5-813b-37f3a6ca4d97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/1e16bf38-5261-48e5-813b-37f3a6ca4d97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Wednesday, claiming it captured the chilling final second before Border Patrol agents fatally shot 37-year-old Alex Pretti during an altercation in Minneapolis--yet the dramatic image was AI-generated, featuring a headless agent and misattributing the incident to ICE.

* **Misinformation Spreads** Outlets like MS NOW admitted using an AI-enhanced headshot of Pretti in coverage, while the viral poster originated from online posts shortly after the Saturday shooting, highlighting AI's role in fueling political outrage.

# Woke tech titans slam ICE's crackdown
OpenAI's Sam Altman and Apple's Tim Cook broke silence on the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, **[criticizing ICE tactics as excessive](https://substack.com/redirect/6dd0a31a-3714-498a-968d-e8c48a6d636a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** following the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti in Minneapolis and calls for de-escalation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6dd0a31a-3714-498a-968d-e8c48a6d636a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Altman Draws Distinction** OpenAI CEO told employees ICE actions go beyond deporting violent criminals, stressing the need to differentiate and push back against overreach while affirming support for U.S. values and hope for presidential unity.
* **Cook Seeks Calm** Apple CEO expressed heartbreak over Minneapolis events in an internal memo, urging de-escalation, emphasizing dignity for all, and noting he privately shared concerns directly with President Trump.
* **Employee Pressure Mounts** Over 450 tech workers from Google, Meta, Salesforce, and OpenAI signed a letter demanding companies withdraw ICE from cities, cancel contracts, and condemn violence amid broader corporate calls for restraint.

* * *
# Wisconsin brewery vows free beer for Trump death party
A progressive Wisconsin brewery **[sparked national outrage](https://substack.com/redirect/e397cba9-2d82-4008-8057-bfa3b088f6cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by promising free beer all day long on the day President Donald Trump dies, posting the offer on Facebook last week and pledging to honor it "in a few months" with proof of the event.
"Show us this post when it happens in a few months and we'll make good on that promise," the company **[wrote on social media.](https://substack.com/redirect/9b8a640d-c059-4005-91af-0f10ffa4b378?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e397cba9-2d82-4008-8057-bfa3b088f6cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b8a640d-c059-4005-91af-0f10ffa4b378?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Outrage follows provocative post** The January 22 Facebook announcement from Minocqua Brewing Company drew thousands of reactions, with critics slamming it as disgusting.
* **Anti-Trump activism boosts sales** The openly anti-Trump brewery, owned by Kirk Bangstad, has faced boycotts from distributors but reports a sales spike from media coverage of the controversial free beer promise.
* **Defiant response to critics** The company mocked Fox News and other outlets as propaganda, shared journalists' contacts for backlash, and joked about pouring more free beer "when his blood clot finally moves."

body:
Republicans continue to pass funding for a rogue, violent agency.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124308630/598212719/-153530995?refcode=EM_F_260129ICE_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_LOGO&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwODYxMmU0Mi02NmZkLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=w0My6XF0rlllh_aisua0dPXCZ7kpGxty0NOF5bWlnfo=) Peter,

Last year, Republicans in Congress voted to provide ICE with around $75 billion through Trump’s Big Ugly Bill, making them one of the highest-funded federal law enforcement agencies. How did they pay for it? **By slashing funding for healthcare and food assistance programs.** Now, the GOP wants to _further_ fund this violent and rogue agency, and I voted NO on the funding bill.

**If Republicans cared about the American people, they would repeal the additional funding that ICE received and put it back into SNAP.**

We can’t continue to let ICE commit abuses with no accountability, no respect for the law, and no regard for civil rights. And we can’t continue to let right-wing Republicans get away with putting Trump’s tariff taxes on the American people, making healthcare premiums skyrocket, and forcing families to go hungry.

subject: Statement from WAGOP Chairman Rep. Jim Walsh: When leaders respond by inflaming emotions, they don't protect the public. 01.28.26
body:
Statement from WAGOP Chairman Rep. Jim Walsh: When leaders respond by inflaming emotions, they don't protect the public. 01.28.26

| | | | | [|
---](https://wsrp.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be1a8605f1118163852707f35&id=c762948255&e=6a281f566d)
| | | | | |

Greetings All—

Below, please find a statement from Washington State Republican Party (WAGOP) Chairman Rep. Jim Walsh on Governor Bob Ferguson's reckless and incendiary rhetoric. Instead of investigating allegations of widespread fraud at daycares throughout the state, the governor is deflecting by demonizing federal immigration enforcement.
"What's happening around the country should worry every Washingtonian. Protests aimed at federal immigration enforcement are growing, and in some places, they're boiling over into confrontation and violence. When leaders respond by inflaming emotions rather than calming the situation, they don't protect the public—they increase the risk that someone will get hurt."Gov. Bob Ferguson is choosing escalation.

"He rushed out a heated message about a deadly incident tied to a federal operation in Minnesota before the facts were clear, then used it to rally people rather than urge restraint. That approach is reckless. It tells activists the governor wants a fight - and it rewards the loudest voices pushing the hardest."At the same time, Ferguson is pressuring the Legislature to pass a bill banning law enforcement officers from wearing masks. And separate legislation would block Washington agencies from hiring former ICE officers. Those are serious proposals with real consequences for public safety and public trust - and they deserve a level-headed debate, not afear-driven campaign built on outrage and viral talking points.

"Washington State Attorney General Nick Brown is moving in the same direction. Instead of focusing on keeping Washington safe, he's amplifying the most extreme rhetoric and encouraging a posture of confrontation with the federal government.

"Here's the problem: when the governor and the attorney general frame federal agents as the enemy and act like street conflict is proof of virtue, they don't just 'take a stand.' They help create the conditions for chaos. They make it more likely that Washington becomes the next flashpoint. And they put a target on our communities, our local officers and our families.

"Washington can protect constitutional rights and demand accountability without encouraging lawlessness. If federal officials come to Washington, state leaders should be working to prevent violence - pushing for cooperation where possible, clear boundaries where needed, and a simple message to the public: protest peacefully, and don't interfere with law enforcement operations.

"That's leadership. What we're seeing from Ferguson and Brown is the opposite.

"Ferguson and Brown are the Thelma and Louise on this issue. They're irrational and encouraging lawlessness. It's surreal. They're free to drive themselves off the cliff. We can't let them take all Washingtonians with them."

---

Hi there,

I wanted you to be one of the first to hear the news: I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota. **This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other.**

[**_I’m going to tell you why in a moment. But first: Will you help us get off to a strong start by splitting a donation between my campaign and Lisa Blunt Rochester?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124308895/598213593/-90010348?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.01.29_Klobuchar-Launch_B1_F1_S1_C1_U1_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85Mjg3NiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYzk3M2RkMC02NmZkLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mPPA_dDmlztWr9rPSZKXlVcLodMGmOKLnSoC9dyLvrk=)

I’m not going to sugar coat it -- Minnesota has been through a lot.

The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. Three thousand ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America’s heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will.

**These moments call for grit and resilience.** I’ve learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up.

And grit? I learned that from my family. I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn’t be where I am today without them.

**T****hese times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state.

I led our state’s biggest prosecutors’ office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law.

**I will do my job without fear or favor. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful. That’s what I did as prosecutor. That’s what I did as senator. And that’s what I will do as your governor.**

I believe we must stand up for what’s right. And fix what’s wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love.

And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder.

_But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support._

**This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change.**

[**_So please: Will you support my campaign for governor with a donation today? Your contribution will be split with Lisa Blunt Rochester._**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124308897/598213596/-90010348?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.01.29_Klobuchar-Launch_B1_F1_S1_C1_U1_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85Mjg3NiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYzk3M2RkMC02NmZkLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=mPPA_dDmlztWr9rPSZKXlVcLodMGmOKLnSoC9dyLvrk=)

**I like my job in the Senate. But I love our state more than any job.** I love the people of Minnesota. And Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor.

Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us.

To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do -- and that’s why I’m asking you to join us.

| | Patriot,
---
| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn't a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal -- the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God's grace. **

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." **_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.

When you read it, you will hear Charlie's voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie's hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

Friend, Last weekend, thousands of Americans came out in the freezing cold to protest in their cities against ICE. body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)
I want to tell you about a special campus just outside of Houston: Prairie View A&M;, or as every Panther calls it, "The Hill."
PVAMU isn’t just a university. It’s a Texas powerhouse that has been ground zero for voting rights for over fifty years. But like many HBCUs, it’s also been under constant attack. Between historic underfunding and aggressive, targeted moves to silence student voices, the community here has had to fight for every inch of progress. (Check out **[this article**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/67485?t=3&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3) recounting the history of their voting rights challenges.)
And because it’s out in Waller County (about an hour from the city), it’s often overlooked by the metro political machine that tends to stop at the Houston city limits. **But we know that if we don’t show up in these rural counties, we’re leaving thousands of voices behind.**
At PVAMU, they don’t just study political science... they live it. Every few years, a new generation has to head to the courts or the streets to protect their right to be heard. They are the literal front line for the 26th Amendment.
In an election cycle this critical, we aren’t just registering voters, we’re joining a legacy of defiance and action. That’s why I was so fired up to be out there with our Powered by People volunteers this week. [**And it’s also why I’m asking you to pitch in $3 today to help ensure we can organize and register voters on more campuses throughout Texas.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260129-2.DxIbt7&refcode=ema20260129-240651&t=4&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)
To make sure everything went smoothly, I was up early to get certified as a VDR in Waller County. I actually ran into two of our volunteers, Cindy and Jeanne, at the election office doing the exact same thing! Just the three of us making sure we had the right paperwork so no student gets caught in a technicality.
By the time I got to campus, the energy was high. We spent the day talking to students who are just trying to navigate a system that doesn't always make it easy for them. Some didn’t even know they could vote right there on campus; others were surprised that Texas still doesn't do online registration.
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260129-2.DxIbt7&refcode=ema20260129-240651&t=5&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260129-2.DxIbt7&refcode=ema20260129-240651&t=6&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260129-2.DxIbt7&refcode=ema20260129-240651&t=7&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)
**The real work isn't just registering them to vote and moving on. It’s staying in touch.** With their permission, we keep their numbers so we can text them about election dates and ID laws or help them find their polling place. Whatever it takes to make sure they actually get to the finish line and cast their ballot.
By the end of the day, we had _102_ solid conversations. We helped _43_ students register and verified the voter registration status for another _59_.
That’s _102_ people who now have someone—a real person—they can actually reach out to if they run into a hurdle in Waller County. And tomorrow, our volunteers are back at it on campuses in other parts of the state.
[**Your contribution of any amount makes our work on campuses possible. Will you pitch in $3 today to help our organizers, volunteers, and student leaders reach, register, and turn out more voters during this critical election year?**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260129-2.DxIbt7&refcode=ema20260129-240651&t=8&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260129-2.DxIbt7&refcode=ema20260129-240651&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=27&akid=240651%2E444211%2EbQnaW3)**
See you out there,
Aimee Prudhomme
Executive Director, Powered by People

That’s why I was so fired up to be out there with our Powered by People volunteers this week. To make sure everything went smoothly, I was up early to get certified as a VDR in Waller County. I actually ran into two of our volunteers, Cindy and Jeanne, at the election office doing the exact same thing! Just the three of us making sure we had the right paperwork so no student gets caught in a technicality. By the time I got to campus, the energy was high. We spent the day talking to students who are just trying to navigate a system that doesn't always make it easy for them. Some didn’t even know they could vote right there on campus; others were surprised that Texas still doesn't do online registration. The real work isn't just registering them to vote and moving on. It’s staying in touch. With their permission, we keep their numbers so we can text them about election dates and ID laws or help them find their polling place. Whatever it takes to make sure they actually get to the finish line and cast their ballot. By the end of the day, we had 102 solid conversations. We helped 43 students register and verified the voter registration status for another 59. That’s 102 people who now have someone—a real person—they can actually reach out to if they run into a hurdle in Waller County. And tomorrow, our volunteers are back at it on campuses in other parts of the state. See you out there, Aimee Prudhomme Executive Director, Powered by People

body:
To accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124309898/598216956/-923472234?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-01-29_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOThjNDM3MDgtNmFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4LP0kdIjnAHB9ifO4fbVBlj7OkK-jE9BQRHxbawJ8gk=)
---
Peter --

I wanted you to be one of the first to hear the news: I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota. **This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other.**

[_**I’m going to tell you why in a moment. But first: Will you help us get off to a strong start by donating to my campaign?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124309899/598216957/-923472234?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-01-29_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOThjNDM3MDgtNmFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4LP0kdIjnAHB9ifO4fbVBlj7OkK-jE9BQRHxbawJ8gk=)

I’m not going to sugar coat it -- Minnesota has been through a lot.

The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. Three thousand ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America’s heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will.

**These moments call for grit and resilience.** I’ve learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up.

And grit? I learned that from my family. I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn’t be where I am today without them.

**These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state.

I led our state’s biggest prosecutors’ office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law.

**I will do my job without fear or favor. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful. That’s what I did as prosecutor. That’s what I did as senator. And that’s what I will do as your governor.**

I believe we must stand up for what’s right. And fix what’s wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love.

And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder.

_But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support._

**This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change.**

[_**So please: Will you support my campaign for governor with a donation today?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124309900/598216958/-923472234?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-01-29_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOThjNDM3MDgtNmFmZC1mMDExLTgzMmYtMDAwZDNhMWYwZTRjIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4LP0kdIjnAHB9ifO4fbVBlj7OkK-jE9BQRHxbawJ8gk=)

**I like my job in the Senate. But I love our state more than any job.** I love the people of Minnesota. And Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor.

Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us.

To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do -- and that’s why I’m asking you to join us.

Amy

Peter Willis,

The brutal violence at the hands of ICE has shaken Minneapolis – and the
nation – to its core.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/34943?source=email-20260129&t=1061&akid=10147%2E5885482%2Egi1ie8 ]Headline: Trump's ICE crackdown faces reckoning as outrage mounts over
Alex Pretti shooting

Trump tried to change the narrative, deploying his border czar to the area
“to report directly to me” and claiming ICE will “leave at some point”.
But the reality is NOTHING has changed for those on the ground living in
the midst of ICE’s terror. So it’s more important than ever to double down
on our fight to get ICE out of all our communities, NOW, before more
violence hits.

Right now, our team – led by our organizer Dieu Do on the ground – has
been on the frontlines of rapid response to support families and get ICE
out. She helped organize the march on Friday that got 200,000 into the
streets in -20 degree weather and a vigil following Pretti’s murder on
Saturday. Folks on the ground like Dieu are seeing the horror unfold every
day — and they need our support.

Despite these efforts to terrorize us into silence, it’s only making us

| | Friend, The Minnesota precinct caucuses are **less than one week away** , and everything we do between now and caucus night will determine how strong our movement is when Republicans gather for caucus on Tuesday, February 3 at 7:00p.m. Caucus night doesn’t run itself. We have to make sure conservatives across southern Minnesota show up, run for delegate to their BPOU convention, and know the ground rules to have their voices heard. That takes real resources—and time is running out. Your hometown caucus is the first step to the endorsing conventions over the next several months where we need to endorse America First conservatives up and down the ballot. That process starts next Tuesday evening. This final stretch is about **turnout and organization**. Minnesota Democrats understand that. They’re already mobilizing. And we can’t afford to be caught flat-footed.That’s why I’m asking you to step up right now and contribute to our **Caucus Fund**.Your support in these final days helps us:
---
* Provide pro-Finstad literature and campaign materials to caucus locations
* Equip caucus volunteers
* Ensure strong conservative caucus turnout across the district

---

| Friends,

America is entering a new chapter in how we think about food and health.

With the release of the new federal nutrition guidelines, there’s growing recognition that the old model of counting calories, fearing protein, and chasing food trends has failed too many people.

What’s been missing from this conversation is muscle.

**Muscle isn’t just about strength or appearance. It’s the foundation of metabolic health, resilience as we age, and long-term independence.** And yet for decades, it’s been overlooked in our national approach to nutrition and wellness.

_That’s why I wrote The Forever Strong Playbook._

**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Democrats advanced a [red flag law expansion](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on a party-line vote, raising due process and Second Amendment concerns, while lawmakers increasingly rely on fees and enterprise funding to [grow government outside TABOR limits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—drawing criticism that voters are being sidelined.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** In Jefferson County, assessor’s office veteran Greg Ketcham entered the race for county assessor, promising [transparency as property values rise](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Colorado Springs took a cultural and economic hit after the Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association [chose Cheyenne, Wyoming, over Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while commentary pushed back on media narratives [blaming climate change for power shutoffs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), arguing utility decisions and infrastructure failures are being ignored.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Winter storm Fern [exposed grid reliability gaps](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) as green energy underperformed, while new polling showed [voters favor stronger immigration enforcement](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) despite media narratives. That divide surfaced in Minnesota, where [anti-ICE protests turned destructive](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), as [Colorado’s growing role in U.S.–Greenland defense](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) highlighted rising Arctic security stakes.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** This week’s commentary warns that [outrage-driven narratives are replacing facts](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in debates over energy, infrastructure, and national security, shielding decision-makers from accountability at moments when clarity matters most.
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, January 29, 2026.
– Team RMV

|

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Red Flag Law Expansion Clears First Senate Committee On Party-Line Vote](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
On Tuesday evening, with a 3-2 vote along party lines, Colorado lawmakers advanced the first bill of the session that wrestles with the debate over gun violence prevention and the right to bear arms.
The Senate State, Veterans, & Military Affairs Committee heard roughly four hours of emotional — and at times, furious — testimony regarding Senate Bill 26-004 (SB26-004), which was introduced by State Senator Tom Sullivan, D — District 27.
“My son, Alex, and 11 others were murdered in the Aurora theater massacre on July 20, 2012,” Sullivan said.
Sullivan’s goal has been to ensure gun violence prevention is a priority at the Colorado State Capitol. He sponsored the original 2019 legislation that enacted the state’s red flag law, which allows certain individuals or agencies to petition a court for an Extreme Risk Protection Order (ERPO).
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado Lawmakers Lean on Fees to Sidestep TABOR Tax Limits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Lawmakers expand “enterprise fees” to bypass TABOR safeguards:** State-run enterprises funded by fees, not taxes, are exempt from TABOR limits, allowing government spending to grow without voter approval.
* **Voters keep rejecting TABOR repeal—but lawmakers keep working around it:** Despite multiple failed repeal attempts, including as recently as 2020, legislators increasingly rely on fees instead of transparent tax hikes.
* **Billions in new revenue proposals clash with taxpayer protections:** While some push to eliminate Colorado’s flat tax and raise billions through higher taxes, TABOR remains the primary check on unchecked government growth.

**[Inside the Assessor’s Office: Why Greg Ketcham Is Running for Jefferson County Assessor](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Insider experience, not politics, drives Ketcham’s run:** Greg Ketcham has spent more than eight years inside the Jefferson County Assessor’s Office, arguing the role should be led by someone who understands property valuation firsthand, not a political appointee.
* **Outdated systems and poor communication hurt taxpayers:** Ketcham says the office relies on rigid two-year cycles and last-minute appeals, leaving property owners confused and frustrated when valuations arrive.
* **Transparency, early outreach, and staff investment are central to reform:** His campaign focuses on clearer communication before deadlines, better-trained appraisers, and restoring public trust without raising taxes or setting rates.

[**“Look at me, not the facts”: How outrage culture drowns out truth**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) **BY MICHAEL HANCOCK | COMMENTARY | JANUARY 28** _Chants are designed to sound simple, righteous, and urgent. They compress emotion into rhythm and repetition. They feel communal. They feel moral. They feel inevitable. When shouted in unison, they create the illusion of truth through volume alone. But chants are rarely the message. They are the cover. Beneath them—almost always—lies something far more dangerous._
[**A closet, a camera and a setup: Tina Peters assaulted in prison then thrown into solitary**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) **BY A.L. GOODWIN | STATE | JANUARY 27** _On the evening of January 18, just after 9:00 p.m., Tina Peters was assaulted inside the La Vista Correctional Facility in Pueblo, Colorado—not in a yard or a common area, but in a narrow janitor’s closet, out of view of surveillance cameras._
[**The Age of Gaslighting Is Ending**](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) **BY C. J. GARBO | COMMENTARY | JANUARY 27** _You don’t get to do this again. You don’t get another George Floyd. You don’t get another COVID. You don’t get another “mostly peaceful” summer of chaos. You don’t get another shutdown. You don’t get another censorship campaign._

The Trump administration has unleashed ICE as a force of terror on our
streets. They raid homes, harass neighbors, and act with impunity. They’ve
shown us over and over: your life, your family, your safety — none of it
matters to them.

And now, there has been another murder by federal agents.

First, Keith Porter was killed by an off-duty ICE agent on New Year’s Eve
outside of his home.

Then, Renee Nicole Good was shot in her car by an ICE agent who claimed
“self-defense,” even though the video and eyewitnesses prove that was a
lie.

Now, Alex Pretti has been murdered by federal agents, his last act a brave
attempt to protect a woman being harassed by ICE.

These murders, clear as day on film, beg the question of what’s happening
behind the walls of detention facilities when agents aren’t being
observed. Dozens of people that we know of died in ICE custody in 2025.
Hundreds more are being mistreated and denied routine medical care.

Innocent people and innocent lives have been stolen by a violent,
unchecked agency. And still, the administration turns a blind eye and
continues to choose violence while families grieve and communities live in
fear.

We cannot stay silent. We cannot wait for another life to be taken. It’s
time to abolish ICE and hold the Trump administration accountable.

* * *
This episode of **AMPED UP** opened with urgency and moral clarity as hosts [Cliff Schecter](https://open.substack.com/users/31941177-cliff-schecter?utm_source=mentions) and [David Shuster](https://open.substack.com/users/16891317-david-shuster?utm_source=mentions) examined the escalating federal crackdown in Minneapolis and what it revealed about the Trump administration's approach to power, force, and accountability. From the outset, the hosts framed the moment not as an isolated abuse, but as part of a longer and deeply American pattern--one that demanded historical context and civic reckoning.
To help unpack those stakes, Schecter and Shuster were joined by Pulitzer Prize-winning columnist [Eugene Robinson](https://open.substack.com/users/648386-eugene-robinson?utm_source=mentions), whose perspective bridged journalism, lived experience, and American history. Robinson brought both clarity and gravity to the discussion, situating the events in Minneapolis within a broader national story about freedom, backlash, and resistance.
* * *
### Six Key Points
**1\. Minneapolis as a National Inflection Point**
Robinson described the federal response in Minneapolis as an "atrocity," arguing that masked federal agents, lethal force, and open defiance of local officials amounted to an attempted occupation of an American city. The panel explored why this moment carried significance far beyond Minnesota.
**2\. Echoes of the Civil Rights Era**
Without resorting to easy or reckless historical comparisons, Robinson explained why Minneapolis echoed moments like Birmingham and Selma--not because the events were identical, but because public resistance and moral clarity had historically forced national change.
**3\. Freedom Gained, Freedom Taken Away**
Drawing from his forthcoming book, **[Freedom Lost, Freedom Won](https://substack.com/redirect/a71c738e-64ef-48a2-9445-0e88ebecb7e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , Robinson outlined a recurring American cycle: hard-won progress followed by organized backlash. From Reconstruction to Jim Crow to the post-civil rights era, freedoms were repeatedly contested rather than secured.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.cddBetmZ_P5woc3aGYemd1LbI8s5kInqjgO3lGAm23Y?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186221507)
* * *
**4\. Personal History as American History**
Robinson shared discoveries from his own family history--enslaved ancestors, Black veterans of World Wars I and II, and long-silenced family stories--arguing that African American history was not a subset of American history, but its core.
**5\. The Collapse of Shared Reality**
The conversation turned to the modern media landscape, focusing on corporate consolidation, disinformation silos, and the erosion of a shared factual baseline. Robinson warned that without common truth, democratic debate itself became nearly impossible.
**6\. What Resistance Had Always Required**
Robinson emphasized that meaningful change had always required people to leave their homes, march, and be visibly counted. Minneapolis, he suggested, might be one of those rare moments capable of forcing the country to confront who it wanted to be.

body:
Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth want to use the power of the White House and the Department of Defense to silence me because they don’t like what I have to say.

| |
---

We’re facing another public fundraising deadline on February 2, where our financial strength will be reported out for anyone to see.
That includes our extreme opponent, Maria Lazar, her multi-millionaire backers, and the right-wing groups already looking for signs of weakness.
That’s why we’ve set an ambitious digital fundraising goal of raising **$50,000** before then.
Hitting this goal does two critical things:
1. It sends a clear signal that Judge Chris Taylor has the grassroots strength to compete — and win — against an extreme opponent bankrolled by right-wing billionaires.

2. It helps deter outside spending. When dark-money groups see real people-powered momentum, they know this race won’t be easy or cheap to buy.

Missing the goal sends the opposite message and invites even more far-right megadonor money into this race.
**We only have a few days to get there, and this is one of those moments where every contribution truly counts.**
[**If you can, chip in $10 or any amount to help reach our $50,000 goal:**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260129_2_ak.8HjMTc&amount=10&refcode=em20260129-1065&t=3&akid=1073%2E294397%2EhNdbGB)

The next round of hearings for Trump’s hand-picked judicial nominees is
almost here. These are judges who will undeniably put Trump’s power over
your rights.

Take a look at the track records for the latest nominees:

* Anna St. John has spent her career attacking LGBTQ+ rights, letting
businesses discriminate, silencing women, and opposing diversity and
equity programs.
* Andrew Davis has gutted corporate accountability, attacked civil
rights, undermined workers and consumers, and fought to weaken voting
protections and environmental safeguards.
* John Thomas Shepherd and Chris Wolfe are far-right ideologues ready to
dismantle protections for everyday people — all under the guise of
“law.”

If these judges are confirmed, decades of rulings will reward corporate
greed, embolden discrimination, and give Trump’s authoritarian tactics a
permanent green light.

And yet, history shows a shocking pattern: 18 Senate Democrats continue to
advance his nominees, waving them through instead of standing up for
democracy.

Every vote they cast is a stamp of approval for Trump’s judicial power
grab.

Demand Justice is sounding the alarm. We’re exposing these judges. We’re
pressuring Senate Democrats to vote NO to Trump’s judicial nominees.

---
_Peter, this is Mazie. My friend Amy Klobuchar is running for governor of Minnesota to stand up for what's right and fix what's wrong. Please read her message below, and I hope you'll consider joining me in supporting her campaign._
* * *
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124310974/598220041/-1050830849?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260129_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlY2UzZTNhZS02ZGZkLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Ta5i8_IGLccFyu-WDXmHNYHs7b-4op2gz5_-o4Uwgng=) Peter -- I wanted you to be one of the first to hear the news: I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota. **This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other.** **[I’m going to tell you why in a moment. But first: Will you help us get off to a strong start by splitting a donation between Mazie Hirono and my campaign?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124310975/598220042/-1050830849?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260129_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlY2UzZTNhZS02ZGZkLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Ta5i8_IGLccFyu-WDXmHNYHs7b-4op2gz5_-o4Uwgng=)** I’m not going to sugar coat it -- Minnesota has been through a lot. The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. Three thousand ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America’s heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will. **These moments call for grit and resilience.** I’ve learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up. And grit? I learned that from my family. I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn’t be where I am today without them. **These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state. I led our state’s biggest prosecutors’ office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law. **I will do my job without fear or favor. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful. That’s what I did as prosecutor. That’s what I did as senator. And that’s what I will do as your governor.** I believe we must stand up for what’s right. And fix what’s wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love. And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder. _But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support._ This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change. **[So please: Will you support my campaign for governor with a donation today? Your contribution will be split with Mazie.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124310976/598220043/-1050830849?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260129_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlY2UzZTNhZS02ZGZkLWYwMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Ta5i8_IGLccFyu-WDXmHNYHs7b-4op2gz5_-o4Uwgng=)** **I like my job in the Senate. But I love our state more than any job.** I love the people of Minnesota. And Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor. Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us. To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do -- and that’s why I’m asking you to join us. Amy

Peter,

In 2012, I was drafted into the NBA--it was a dream come true until I decided to stand up for what I believed in. I've struggled with mental health my entire life, and severe anxiety has been a demon following me at every turn in life. Mental health carried more of a stigma back then; it was hard to open up and take a stand, especially as a first-year player in the NBA. _But, that didn 't stop me from risking everything for something I believed in._

**My story is ultimately one of healing, perseverance, and redemption.**

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=ce68a81f9aa0407796ed182c62c9e608&_e=Yqjqv7VzW0Top5_BTdQMQ2CGT313c5s1gFx94a69H-b_62wNoFQjHJ1cYnJpVhzh7x0xUnEZ3lFb46BLdEqH7ds7_7iqJY1Y92XIHlvPMN90VgPz-Z4v2ZPp-tBFg69iu0uUaBqKEuZRjuQpGk2Vv6xGGlTskAJfbMQqeThtXPto4yJvJmJ913ypQKhBcCnWEj4I8ZVCb66lOtrO1r8MftWKseFVhkWZc63DV8rzrsudlPoEo6Y85VQfP8Tl8hvrtR2yxjqiy4DmLtqPy-pCHUJ2GXiaz7q8qVWhh0jquYGOZzRYnfkmYCTHCqxV3ZmKa6ZyBYi_QTtAxqIQSBVci5agzZpP7Np8a-tcn53umsQtcDK-V1xzoEnHVcmA-DmGCES4G-BpPEvDEGRpUdJHO5dRqmQ71BtbVWBUCWf0dbsvB3h11s8hJqAH2deeV2EYZg2kBdhmFcYG2ESCdRags4BrtGAt_okDDPNdS7rmt6NtNRyVmeEogYeg_uxuv6NN)
At the time, the NBA didn't have any policies to support players' mental health. A grueling 82-game season will weigh on anyone--the best athletes in the world included. As someone who has dealt with an extreme level of anxiety growing up, being thrust onto one of the biggest stages in the world at 21 years old was challenging, to say the least. That's why I decided to speak out and open a dialogue with the NBA about mental health. It was a huge risk at the time, but one that I believed was worth it. I hoped I could help other players who were struggling get the resources they needed.

I did. Despite my speaking out resulting in a huge divide between myself and the NBA, causing me to give up my childhood dream and move over to Canada's professional basketball league, I still think it was worth it. **If I had to, I would do it all again, no questions asked. Now, the NBA has a policy for players ' mental health, and I like to think that I started the conversation to make that happen.**

Throughout the process, my name was dragged through the mud by the Industrial Media Complex. As I said, in 2012, there was a much different stigma about mental health than there is today. But I put my name, my career, and my life on the line to stand up for myself and other players who kept silent because it was bigger than basketball.

**_Today, I have a simple message for anyone struggling with mental health, including our troops, veterans, children, and all Americans: there 's no shame in asking for help, and there's no shame in standing up for yourself. If I could do it, so can you._**

But now that I'm running for Senate, my story is resurfacing, and I'm being attacked by the Radical Left. This race is one of the most important Senate races in 2026, but the mainstream media won't take me seriously. [**Day in and day out, I’m told that I don’t have a chance to win in Minnesota.**](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=ce68a81f9aa0407796ed182c62c9e608&_e=Yqjqv7VzW0Top5_BTdQMQ2CGT313c5s1gFx94a69H-b_62wNoFQjHJ1cYnJpVhzh7x0xUnEZ3lFb46BLdEqH7ds7_7iqJY1Y92XIHlvPMN90VgPz-Z4v2ZPp-tBFg69iu0uUaBqKEuZRjuQpGk2VvwXFheMFriIhxcRizClkHcTbE1ma66HUGkInQuVDyyt1oBU-ZYjD-0Vct0ZOzyZaIORjEKMp85Ii0ZOF3JyQaKY10y0ng8flRv5ZxDwk4IYOpLqFSXwK-Hw_RP4k8-LNRGfnOmbZwgdqu95-mI0teG8K49wjd6bQiROEpnp4v7yRNJWmmrQz8oOc1VkKRNc1l0bP_bcp8XnnXvM-hZaFNkuhHe3nr8TVhwpCnVtSb58j5S1ClyrVEc6BrCody6woUErh_PauVcf29fcXQ5EDOaEYDfUi5atgTXeW34B7vVMfU3oL7q-KSwi4xb2xnPUX7oQNk-vzBjf_H9gSoOVEGKsXVXTVuNK7hC4z78S08C9M)

**Just like when I fought and won in 2012, I will fight and win in 2026.**
Democrats are spending MILLIONS of dollars protecting my Radical Opponent, Peggy Flanagan. Every hour that Democrats attack me and suppress my voice in the media without my campaign having the ability to refute their lies with our own ads, I'm at a huge disadvantage.

clean_body: The industrial media complex attacks me for this | Peter, In 2012, I was drafted into the NBA--it was a dream come true until I decided to stand up for what I believed in. I've struggled with mental health my entire life, and severe anxiety has been a demon following me at every turn in life. Mental health carried more of a stigma back then; it was hard to open up and take a stand, especially as a first-year player in the NBA. But, that didn 't stop me from risking everything for something I believed in. My story is ultimately one of healing, perseverance, and redemption. At the time, the NBA didn't have any policies to support players' mental health. A grueling 82-game season will weigh on anyone--the best athletes in the world included. As someone who has dealt with an extreme level of anxiety growing up, being thrust onto one of the biggest stages in the world at 21 years old was challenging, to say the least. That's why I decided to speak out and open a dialogue with the NBA about mental health. It was a huge risk at the time, but one that I believed was worth it. I hoped I could help other players who were struggling get the resources they needed. I did. Despite my speaking out resulting in a huge divide between myself and the NBA, causing me to give up my childhood dream and move over to Canada's professional basketball league, I still think it was worth it. If I had to, I would do it all again, no questions asked. Now, the NBA has a policy for players ' mental health, and I like to think that I started the conversation to make that happen. Throughout the process, my name was dragged through the mud by the Industrial Media Complex. As I said, in 2012, there was a much different stigma about mental health than there is today. But I put my name, my career, and my life on the line to stand up for myself and other players who kept silent because it was bigger than basketball. Today, I have a simple message for anyone struggling with mental health, including our troops, veterans, children, and all Americans: there 's no shame in asking for help, and there's no shame in standing up for yourself. If I could do it, so can you. But now that I'm running for Senate, my story is resurfacing, and I'm being attacked by the Radical Left. This race is one of the most important Senate races in 2026, but the mainstream media won't take me seriously. Just like when I fought and won in 2012, I will fight and win in 2026. Democrats are spending MILLIONS of dollars protecting my Radical Opponent, Peggy Flanagan. Every hour that Democrats attack me and suppress my voice in the media without my campaign having the ability to refute their lies with our own ads, I'm at a huge disadvantage. | THE PEOPLE ARE COMING! Thank you, Royce White PAID FOR BY ROYCE WHITE FOR SENATE P.O. Box 5473 Hopkins, MN 55343 Copyright (C) 2026 Royce White For Senate, All rights reserved.
